findings.description: parse_rows now returns a generator. Line 35 iterates it fully to build `rejected`, so the later `for row in rows` loop at line 39 sees an exhausted iterator and imports nothing. Every import reports created=0 and updated=0 while silently dropping all valid contacts. The previous list return value made the double iteration safe.
findings.suggestion: Materialise the rows with `rows = list(parse_rows(lines))`. This also keeps the check-before-write guarantee. For true streaming of large files, validate in a first pass over a re-openable source and write in a second pass.

findings.description: parse_rows is now a generator function, so the header validation no longer runs when it is called. It runs on the first `next()`. The ValueError for missing columns still propagates out of import_csv in practice, but any caller that calls parse_rows outside a try block and iterates later will see the error at an unexpected place. Callers also cannot rely on validation having happened once parse_rows returns.
findings.suggestion: Split into an eager function that validates the header and returns an inner generator, or document and handle the lazy behaviour.
